title: Affine chart rings of finite dominant maps with normal base
statement: Let $q:V\to B$ be a finite dominant morphism of integral schemes [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]. Suppose $B$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and every local ring of $B$ is an integrally closed domain. Let $B=\bigcup_iU_i$ be any affine open cover with nonempty $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}(A_i)$ and Noetherian $A_i$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Then every inverse image $q^{-1}(U_i)$ is a nonempty affine open $\operatorname{Spec}(C_i)$ of $V$, and the restricted morphism $q^{-1}(U_i)\to U_i$ is induced by an injective ring map $\varphi_i:A_i\to C_i$. Each $A_i$ is a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], each $C_i$ is a domain, and $C_i$ is a finitely generated $A_i$-module via $\varphi_i$. Such a cover of $B$ exists.

This is the affine-chart preparation for more-morphisms.tex Tag 0F32, lemma-quasi-finite-Noetherian-universally-open, finite normal case.

proof.text: By [pqf-def-locnoeth], $B$ has an affine open cover with Noetherian coordinate rings. Discard empty members; the remaining opens still cover $B$, since an empty set contains no point. This proves the last assertion. Now fix any cover as in the statement and any index $i$.

Write $U=U_i=\operatorname{Spec}(A_i)$. Since $q(V)$ is dense in $B$, it meets the nonempty open $U$ by [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]; hence $W=q^{-1}(U)$ is nonempty. It is open by continuity. The finite-morphism definition [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] gives $W=\operatorname{Spec}(C_i)$ affine and the associated ring map $\varphi_i:A_i\to C_i$ making $C_i$ a finite $A_i$-module. Both $U$ and $W$ are nonempty affine opens of integral schemes, so [def-pc-integral-scheme] says that both $A_i$ and $C_i$ are domains.

To prove injectivity, suppose $a\ne0$ in $A_i$ and $\varphi_i(a)=0$. The zero ideal of the domain $A_i$ is a prime not containing $a$, so the basic open $D(a)\subseteq U$ is nonempty. It is also open in $B$, and dominance gives $v\in V$ with $q(v)\in D(a)$; necessarily $v\in W$. Let $Q\subset C_i$ be its prime. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-stalk-localization], the image point corresponds to $\varphi_i^{-1}(Q)$. But $\varphi_i(a)=0\in Q$, so $a\in\varphi_i^{-1}(Q)$, contradicting $q(v)\in D(a)$. The kernel is zero, which proves injectivity.

proof.text: For each maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\subset A_i$, take its point $x\in U_i$. The affine-open stalk theorem [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] identifies $(A_i)_{\mathfrak m}$ with $\mathcal O_{B,x}$. The latter is an integrally closed domain by hypothesis, so the localization is a normal domain, in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. The already proved domain property of $A_i$ and [lem-weil-pbc-normal-domain-of-local-normal] now show that $A_i$ is a normal domain. Its Noetherian property is part of the chosen-cover hypothesis. Since $i$ was arbitrary, all the required assertions hold for every chart.
